_comment: TERRAIN profiles (plan-region-primitive.md D2/D12/C3). A profile is a named bag of CLIENT-SIDE presentation properties a shape points at by name; the server never reads any of it. These are worn by the shapes that paint the GROUND — zone.regions, zone.paths and zone.polygons, plus the outlineProfile of the latter two. The AIR over an area is the sibling file, atmosphere-profiles.json, and the two tables are deliberately SEPARATE so neither vocabulary can be named on the other's shape. This file is the single source of truth for its half: the client imports it, and tools/tiled/generate-palette.mjs reads it to build Tiled's AuraTerrainProfile dropdown, so a profile added here is offerable in the editor without anyone maintaining a second list. A profile that omits a property is TRANSPARENT to it (D0): the next containing region answers, and failing that the shipped default.
_comment_split: ⭐ THE SPLIT IS THE POINT (PO 2026-09-15). One shared table meant ONE Tiled dropdown holding both vocabularies, so naming a ground profile on an atmosphere drew nothing and naming an atmosphere profile on a region painted grey mud — L15, and it cost a session. Two files means two enums (AuraProfile here, AuraAtmosphereProfile there), and the mistake is no longer a dropdown entry at all. ⛔ So do NOT author `darkness`, `haze` or `sight` in this file: nothing reads them off a terrain profile, TerrainProfile does not declare them, and Regions.test.ts fails if one appears. They belong next door.
_comment_colors: Colours are ground fill, drawn under the terrain blobs. ⚑ Every value here is [PLACEHOLDER] and safe to change forever - it is data, not code, and no test pins any of it. NAMES are the only mildly sticky part: a region in api/zones/*.json names its profile, so a rename means fixing every region that names it.
_comment_c3: The set was ruled 2026-08-25 (C3, the D16 look sitting): 8 families x 2, base + variation, in authored order because that is the order the Tiled dropdown offers. ⭐ EVERY profile is intended to carry a TEXTURE eventually (C3 ruling, D18) - since C4 every one does. ⚑ A profile is a MATERIAL, not a place: many separate forests share `Forest`, which is why a quest-addressable area cannot be a profile name (§11).
_comment_texture: C4: `texture` names a seamless tile BY FILE STEM in frontend/src/features/regions/assets/ground (see the README there for provenance and what each pick is); `scale` is texture->world, so 0.35 draws a 750px tile over 262 world px - the SENSITIVE knob (§4.8), tuned per profile by eye. ⚑ D14: `color` under a `texture` is the FALLBACK and NEVER a tint - it is what paints if the file is missing or still loading, which is why every profile keeps one. A texture naming a file that is not there costs that region its tile and nothing else.
_comment_paths: plan-world-paths.md C1: the last three profiles are worn by PATHS and POLYGON OUTLINES (zone.paths, zone.polygons), not regions - an open polyline STROKED rather than a closed polygon filled. Same table, same keys, same D14 fallback, because in Pixi 8 a stroke style IS a fill style. ⚑ Their `blend` is deliberately NOT the uniform 1.5 above: a band is measured in world units, so 1.5 on a 2.5-unit road is a soft edge wider than the road. [PLACEHOLDER] like everything here, and precisely what the look sitting is for. ⚑ Water names a PLACEHOLDER tile generated by tools/make-water-tile.mjs (deterministic, re-runnable); its colour is the same #2a63a8, so the river does not change hue when the texture lands. ⛔ There is no `Bridge` profile: a bridge is a PROP (D6).
_comment_scroll: plan-world-paths.md C3: `scroll` drifts the profile's TILE, in world UNITS PER SECOND, as a TilingSprite whose tilePosition is nudged per frame - two number writes per surface and nothing rebuilt. Absent or {0,0} = still, which is every profile but Water, so the feature costs exactly zero until authored. ⚑ It moves the TEXTURE, not the shape: the river stays where it was drawn. ⚑ A profile with `texture: null` (or naming a missing file) animates NOTHING - a flat colour has no visible phase, and D14's fallback stays a still colour by design. ⚑ ONE world vector per profile, so every river on `Water` flows the same way regardless of which direction it was drawn (D9) - the accepted limit, since direction is geometry and this table is material. Values [PLACEHOLDER]: at scale 0.35 one 750px tile spans ~2.19 units, so 0.4 u/s repeats about every 5.5 s.
_comment_blend: C5: `blend` is the width of the soft border in WORLD UNITS, per PROFILE (D2) and never per region. 0 = a hard edge, the world C4 shipped and the way D5's look stays expressible. ⭐ D23 (PO 2026-09-29, amends D22): a REGION's fade lies wholly OUTSIDE its polygon - solid up to the line drawn in Tiled, fading out past it (¾ of the blend, so a region reaches ~1.1 u past its line at 1.5) - so two regions painted side by side close their seam with no ground showing. `blendOutward: false` on a profile puts that profile back on D22's centred ramp. A POLYGON is centred by default and a profile can opt it outward with `true`; paths, outlines and clearings never read the key. A region feathers its OWN edge and knows nothing of its neighbours, so region-meets-region and region-meets-bare-land are one code path. ⚑ [PLACEHOLDER] like every value here: 1.5 is a uniform starting point for the look sitting, not a decision. ⚑ plan-ground-noise.md W1c: a positive blend narrower than the mask can draw is WIDENED to the finest it can (≈ 0.125 u desktop, 0.25 u on a phone), never dropped to a hard edge; only 0 is hard.
_comment_wobble: plan-ground-noise.md W1 + W1b (D3): three keys BREAK UP an edge, each moving ONE look, and none of them touches `blend`, which is the fade and only the fade. `wobbleReach` (world units) is how far the edge WANDERS either side of the authored line; absent = straight and no extra bake pass. `wobbleSize` (world units) is the LUMP size; absent = derived from the reach. `wobbleRoughness` (0…1) is how FRAYED each lump is: 0 smooth, 1 the fine octaves as strong as the coarse; absent = 0.5. ⭐ Any mix is legal: a `blend: 0` edge with a reach is CRISP and wandering (a cut plot, a rocky shore), a wide blend with no reach is a clean biome fade. ⭐ The noise is keyed to WORLD position, so the 50 % line still sits on the authored one on average (D22), two abutting surfaces agree, and the full-screen map draws the same edge. ⛔ W1's 0…1 `wobble` is RETIRED, not aliased: Regions.test.ts fails on any key the parser does not know. ⚑ Road, Water and the four field profiles carry W1's look TRANSLATED into the new keys (same fade, same wander, same lump), not retuned. Out-of-range values are dropped, not clamped. Every value [PLACEHOLDER].
_comment_overlay: plan-ground-noise.md W2: `overlay` paints a SECOND profile over this one in world-keyed noise PATCHES — stones showing through grass. `{ "profile": <a profile in this file>, "coverage": 0…1, "size": <world units>, "roughness": 0…1 }`. It names another profile as `outlineProfile` does, so the patches take THAT profile's texture, scale, colour (D14) and drift (D5); its own blend, wobble and overlay are ignored, so an overlay never recurses. `coverage` is roughly the share covered (exact at 0, ½, 1). `size` is the patch size and `roughness` how frayed a patch's outline is, the overlay's OWN keys (D4), never the base's wobble keys; absent = 1.5 u and 0.5. ⭐ The patches are cut out of the surface's own mask, so they fade out at its edge, wobble and all, and never spill past it; on a HARD edge (no blend, no wobble) the shape's own geometry clips them, so they reach the crisp edge and stop there. ⭐ World-keyed, so the full-screen map draws the same patches, and two touching surfaces with the same overlay and `size` usually line up across their seam (not guaranteed: a very large shape can bake coarser and floor its patch size). ⚑ An overlay naming a profile that is not in this file draws NOTHING (Regions.test.ts fails on one). ⚑ Cost: one more mask texture and one more masked draw per overlaid surface; none for a profile without one. Every value [PLACEHOLDER]. ⭐ `FieldsForestBlend` is `Fields` with `Forest` patches (PO 2026-09-27): a SECOND profile rather than an overlay on `Fields`, so every existing field stays as authored and the blend is painted only where a region names it.
_comment_fields: ⭐ THE CULTIVATED SET, worn by POLYGONS rather than by regions (content-zone-design-guide.md §2.2: a field plot is a non-blocking polygon lying on the Fields region, which is what the layer order already says — ground, then regions, then polygons, then paths, so a plot sits on the field and a road still runs across the plot). ⛔ Their `blend` is 0 and that is the whole point: the 1.5 above feathers a BIOME edge, and a feathered field plot is a contradiction — straight parallel edges are the visual language of farmland, and anywhere else in the game straight is wrong. ⭐ EACH MATERIAL SHIPS TWICE, once per row DIRECTION, because a profile has no rotation knob: `texture`/`scale`/`blend`/`color`/`scroll` and nothing else, so every plot wearing one profile has its rows running the same way in world space. Authoring a patchwork means alternating the two, which is also what real farmland looks like. ⚑ A diagonal variant is one constant block in tools/make-field-tiles.mjs away (any INTEGER wave pair is a legal direction). ⛔ THEIR `scale` IS 1, NOT the 0.35 every other profile uses, and it is the one number here that is not free: at 0.35 a 750 px tile covers 2.19 u, so FIVE copies cross a 1280 px screen — and rows are the worst thing to repeat at that pitch, because a directional pattern is what the eye locks onto first. The first cut shipped that way and read as corduroy with a seam every two metres (PO: "repeating way too often"). At 1 a tile covers 6.25 u and repeats ~1.7 times, with the furrows re-cut so the spacing on screen is unchanged (11 rows, 0.57 u; wheat drills 0.5 u). ⚑ Both were then tuned against REFERENCE IMAGES the PO supplied: the plough is soft broad streaks with dark blotches rather than crisp ridges, and the wheat is a dense flock of tiny tufts over visible earth - which is why Wheat's colour is #b08f4c and not the straw it started as, the mean-colour check in the generator having caught the drift. ⚑ tools/make-field-tiles.mjs READS this value and derives every feature size from it, so changing it here and re-running the script keeps the furrows 0.45 u apart and only moves the repeat. All values [PLACEHOLDER].
_comment_coast: ⭐ THE CLIFFTOP (PO 2026-10-03: *a pale irish coast grass texture … blended over a limestone rock, a cliff feel should exist*). `Coastal Cliff` is BURREN LIMESTONE under a COAST GRASS overlay, the FieldsForestBlend pattern: the slabs show through the sward in noise patches, so the bluff reads as rock with grass on it rather than as a lawn or a quarry. It used to borrow `pd196`, the Mountains tile, and so was the same ground as a mountain range. ⭐ `Limestone` and `Coast Grass` are profiles in their own right (an overlay can only name a profile), so either can paint a region alone. Both tiles come out of tools/make-cellular-tiles.mjs. ⚑ `coverage` 0.72 is the grass share: lower it and the bluff gets rockier. All values [PLACEHOLDER].
_comment_liquids: ⭐ `Bog` and `Lava` are `Water`'s siblings and come out of the SAME generator (tools/make-water-tile.mjs), which builds RIDGED fields — a smooth wave sum pushed through `1 - |sin|` raised to a power, so the same machinery makes a wave crest at sharpness 4.2, a broad scum blotch at 1.4 and a thin bright CRACK at 7. ⚑ One knob spanning three materials that look nothing alike, which is why they share a script rather than each getting one. ⭐ A BOG IS WATER WITH EVERY WATER CUE REMOVED: its waves are ISOTROPIC where Water's are clustered into a swell (a bog does not flow, so a dominant direction would be a lie about the material), its sharpness is too low for anything to read as a crest, and its drift is 0.04 u/s against Water's 0.2 — a river creeps, a bog barely moves at all. ⛔ `Lava`'s `color` is THE ONE PLACE THIS TABLE DELIBERATELY BREAKS THE MATCH-THE-TILE RULE, and it is worth knowing why: every other profile's colour is its tile's dominant tone, so the hue does not jump when the texture lands. Lava's dominant tone is the near-black of cooled crust — and D14 paints `color` as a FLAT wash whenever the tile is missing or still loading, so honouring the rule would make lava read as ASPHALT in exactly the moments a player most needs to recognise it. ⚑ That mattered little while this was decoration; it matters a lot now that `docs/plan-area-effects.md` makes lava something that can kill you, so legibility wins and the hue jumps. ⚑ Both are worn by POLYGONS (a lava lake, a bog pool) and by PATHS (a lava river) — same table, same keys, exactly as Water already is. ⚑ Every number [PLACEHOLDER].
_comment_fence: ⭐ THE FIRST **DIRECTIONAL** PROFILE — WRONG unless its path authors `alignTexture: true`, which TURNS the tile to run along the path and REGISTERS it across the path (world.Path.AlignTexture). Every other texture here is world-aligned and had to look the same in every direction; a fence has a direction. ⛔ NOT A DROP-IN: forget the flag and the rails lie ACROSS the fence, with nothing to warn you. ⚑ AUTHOR ONE PATH PER STRAIGHT LEG — angle and anchor both come from the longest segment, so a bend gets its dominant leg and the short one is wrong; that is also how a fence is built, the corner being where the post goes. ⛔ AUTHOR THE PATH AT width 0.40, AND THIS PROFILE S `scale` IS NOT FREE. Unlike every other entry here, the tile s PIXEL HEIGHT encodes the fence: fence-placeholder.png is 750x96 with the fence in its middle 48 rows, and registration lands the middle row on the centreline, so at scale 1 a 0.40-unit stroke reveals exactly the fence and nothing of the next copy. Anything up to 0.80 is still safe (the margin is transparent); past that the next copy creeps in, and changing `scale` rescales the fence itself. tools/make-fence-tile.mjs READS this value, derives post spacing from it and refuses a tile that would not fit. ⭐ It is RGBA, alone among the ground tiles, because THE GAPS ARE THE FENCE — the first cut was opaque and read as a boardwalk (PO: not like a fence at all). ⛔ `blend` is 0: a feathered fence is a contradiction. All values [PLACEHOLDER].
_comment_cliff: ⭐ THE SECOND DIRECTIONAL PROFILE, and it is Fence read again with one divergence. Everything the fence comment says about alignTexture applies verbatim: WRONG without the flag, one path per straight leg, and the tile PIXEL HEIGHT is load-bearing because registration lands the middle row on the centreline. cliff-placeholder.png is 720x320 with the cliff drawn in its middle 240 rows, so at scale 1 a 2.0-unit stroke reveals exactly the cliff. ⛔ AUTHOR THE PATH ALONG THE MID-FACE, NOT ALONG THE LIP — the reveal is symmetric about the centreline, so a path drawn on the edge itself buries the foot and the shadow. ⭐ WHICH SIDE THE LAND IS ON IS THE WINDING ORDER, and nothing warns: draw the run the other way and the cliff faces inland. ⭐ THE ONE DIVERGENCE FROM FENCE: this tile DOES bake a shadow, where the fence refuses one. A sun shadow points a fixed way in WORLD space while the tile turns, so it would swing — but what is baked here is the face OCCLUDING the ground at its own foot, which is defined relative to the face and rotates with it correctly. A real sun shadow for a cliff is still its own world-aligned shape. ⛔ `blend` is 0: a cliff edge is an object, not a material gradient. ⚑ The same profile is meant to wear a MOUNTAIN, drawn as a CLOSED path ringing the massif — the rim and the coastal drop are one tile, which is the whole reason it is worth generating. All values [PLACEHOLDER], and the tile is a PLACEHOLDER: real art wanted.
_comment_cliff_smooth: ⭐ THE SAME CLIFF WITH ITS DETAIL TAKEN OUT, and it exists because of a property of the RIBBON MESH rather than a taste call. Arc-length UVs stretch on the outside of every bend and compress on the inside — which is what a real stratum does, and what lets ONE path cross any number of corners — but that stretch is only VISIBLE if the texture carries detail fine enough to see it warp. A facet mosaic warps legibly; a near-uniform face cannot, because there is nothing in it to distort. ⛑ PO on the facet cut: *the cliffside is perhaps too textured to work well with the ribbon path, because it gets warped*. ⚡ IDENTICAL GEOMETRY CONTRACT to `Cliff` — 720x320, the drop in the middle 240 rows, `width` 2.0, `alignTexture` required — so the two are INTERCHANGEABLE: swap the profile name on a path and nothing else moves. That is the point of shipping both rather than choosing blind. ⚡ Its edges are also far gentler (PO: *a little too jagged*): one octave less on the lip, a third the amplitude, and a foot that dissolves rather than crumbling. All values [PLACEHOLDER], tile is a PLACEHOLDER: real art wanted.
_comment_shoreline: ⭐ THE THIRD DIRECTIONAL PROFILE, and Cliff's convention read again on purpose: `alignTexture` REQUIRED, and to follow a BEND it also needs `corners: sharp` + `ends: flat` or `point` (only that shape gets the arc-length mesh; the default round corners fall back to the one-matrix stroke, exact on a straight leg and broken past a bend, until plan-world-paths.md §12 chunk B), the tile REGISTERED on the centreline, and the WINDING ORDER deciding the side - land on the side a Cliff puts its lip, sea on the side it puts its foot, so an author who has drawn one coast has drawn both. ⭐ Author it ALONG THE WATER'S EDGE, straddling it: the land half is wet dark sand fading out into whatever the region is, and the tile ENDS at the bright SWASH LINE: the sea half is empty, the Water beneath shows through (the foam lace + second wave line were CUT 2026-10-03, PO: a static ripple looked bad). ⛔ STATIC, no `scroll`: a profile has ONE world drift vector, so anything drifting along one shore would drift INTO the next one round the bay. ⚑ `blend` 0: the tile fades itself by alpha on the land side and ends at the swash line on the sea side. Tile generated by tools/make-shoreline-tile.mjs; all values [PLACEHOLDER].
_comment_cobblestone: ⭐ THE CITY STREET: `Road` paved. A PATH profile (width 2-3 like Road), and a drop-in for Road on any path: the cobbles are ROUNDED and undirected, so it works on a meander and needs no `alignTexture` (coursed setts would). Its tile is tools/make-cellular-tiles.mjs's `cobble` (a Voronoi cut with soft-rounded corners and dirt joints). ⭐ Colour set against its NEIGHBOURS: `City`'s tile (pd141) measures #847d6b, so the street is that warm grey a step darker (reads as paving laid in the plaza, not painted on it) and stays warm so it is not `Wall`'s neutral #7d7d80 laid flat. `color` is the tile's measured mean (the generator asserts it, D14). ⚑ `blend` near-hard with a small wobble: a paved street has a kerb, not a biome fade, and the wobble is the edge stones jutting unevenly. All values [PLACEHOLDER], the tile is a PLACEHOLDER.
_comment_stones: ⭐ THE FIRST OVERLAY MATERIAL (plan-ground-noise.md W2): meant to be named by another profile's `overlay` (none does yet) rather than worn by a shape, though a shape may wear it like any other profile. Its tile is tools/make-cellular-tiles.mjs's `stones`, the road's pebbles turned up until they are the material (≈ 45 % stones), so it is busier than a ground tile may be: a patch shows a piece of it and stops, where a surface repeats it nine times across a screen. `color` is the tile's measured mean (the generator asserts it, D14). All values [PLACEHOLDER], the tile is a PLACEHOLDER.
